ov: Five species of burrowing ground squirrels from the grasslands of North America, named for their bark-like warning call. They live in family groups inside large colonies, and their digging helps renew grass and topsoil.
rg: The Great Plains and grasslands of the western United States, the Canadian Prairies and northern Mexico.
df: Mainly grasses and small seeds, plus forbs, roots, fruit and buds; sometimes insects.
fx: Burrows can have up to six entrances, with mounds used as lookout posts.
Family members greet each other with "kisses" and grooming, but not outsiders.
